timeline.text:
## Vulnerabilities Found and Fixed

**SQL Injection vulnerability** in `ProductMapper.java` — all four methods used `${}` (direct string interpolation) instead of `#{}` (parameterized queries).

| Method | Vulnerable | Fixed |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| `insert` | `'${name}'` | `#{name}` |
| `update` | `'${name}'` | `#{name}` |
| `delete` | `'${name}'` | `#{name}` |
| `select` | `'${name}'` | `#{name}` |

**What changed:**
- `${}` performs raw string concatenation, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., `'; DROP TABLE products; --`)
- `#{}` uses JDBC prepared statement parameters, which properly escape and bind values, preventing SQL injection
- The file also contained the wrong class (ProductService code instead of the mapper interface), which was corrected

The project compiles successfully after the fix.
